findings.note: Matthews had surgery in March 2026 for a grade 3 MCL tear with an expected 12-week recovery. That points to a return by this season, but nothing I found confirms his status for the Oct. 17 game, his practice participation or his current lineup role.

He had his second straight season with a significant absence, finishing 2025-26 with 27 goals in 60 games, and hasn't played a full 82-game season since 2016-17. Durability is a risk, and his scoring before the injury was below his elite peak.
In November 2025 he missed time with a separate lower-body injury after a hit from Zadorov, and had 9 goals in 17 games before it. This adds to his recent string of injuries.

This CBS page links to a related headline, 'Maple Leafs' Auston Matthews: Exits Thursday's game.' I couldn't see the date or details, so it's unverified. If it means the Oct. 15 Buffalo game, he still logged 22:14 and scored. Confirm he's playing tonight before betting.

The Oct. 17 NHL.com preview says Matthews has points in six straight games (13 points in that span) and leads Toronto in goals (6), assists (7) and points (13). Toronto won the first meeting 2-1, though it isn't clear whether Matthews scored.

ESPN lists Matthews as active with 6 goals on 26 shots in 8 games, about 22 minutes a night and 2 power-play goals. His last game against Buffalo was 1 goal on 1 shot. Two goals in one game is still rare even with this usage.

This January 2026 RotoWire/CBS note says Nylander had 75 shots on goal in 37 games in 2025-26. That is about 2.0 per game, which is under the 2.5 line. It is last season's data, and no current-season shot data was found.

This January 2026 CBS note says Nylander had four straight seasons with 250 or more shots, including one with 316. Those totals work out to roughly 3 or more shots per game, but the stretch comes before his lower shot rate in 2025-26.

ESPN reported in January 2026 that Nylander aggravated a recurring lower-body (groin) injury that cost him several stretches last season. No dated October 2026 reporting on his status, the lineup or analyst picks for this game came up, so his current health is unconfirmed.

Rotowire notes from last season (April 2026) say Rossi finished in a top-six, second-line role with power-play time and had 34 points in 48 games. There is no dated 2026-27 lineup, injury or usage news for this game, so the long +330 price is still unexplained.

On September 25, 2026, the Canucks reported that Rossi came to training camp early and feeling good under new head coach Manny Malhotra. It does not confirm his line, power-play role or health for October 17.

In March 2026, Rossi played on the Canucks' first power-play unit on the left half-wall and was described as the line's playmaker. This is old evidence that may not reflect current usage under Malhotra.

Recent report (Oct 12, 2026): McLeod scored his first goal of the season and won 7 of 16 faceoffs in a 5-3 win over Florida, so he is active and centering. It gives no assist count or line update for tonight, and the search found no injury, lineup or analyst-pick news for this game.

In 2025-26 he had 40 assists in 81 regular-season games as Buffalo's second-line center and played on the power play and penalty kill. Against the bet: he had just 4 assists in 13 playoff games, and older notes flag that he shoots very little.

Game log from the 2026 playoff series against Montreal: he had an assist in 3 of 7 games. His ice time dropped to 9:35 and 13:23 in Games 4-5, which suggests his role was cut at times. This is last season's data, not the current one.
